what: KSPLIT (2026-10-25): the blocked contract's weight adjoints -- dW = dY^T X, a call with A transposed whose depth is the batch's rows -- split over their depth into the workspace the state lends: a call at least four K blocks deep (BCIR_MM_KSPLIT_BLOCKS) runs a pool task a K block, each block's product over all of C stored as the kernel's accumulators hold it (BCIR_MM_RAW) into its slice of the room, then a fold job, sixteen rows a task, gives every element its blocks in order with the blocked kernels' epilogue -- the first block's beta scaling, then c + alpha*P block after block -- so every value is the nest's bit for bit; the trainer lends the state's workspace (under a binary32 contract ATT-CONTIG's attention copies, from 1,024 positions) to every blocked GEMM job with a weight adjoint, on the fixed step and the program rail alike (ks_lends), and the unit splits the calls whose partials fit what is left of it
